entries.title: Dynamic-workflow trigger renamed workflow → ultracode · acceptEdits prompts before exec-granting config writes
entries.paragraph: The dynamic-workflow trigger keyword changed from workflow to ultracode — the literal word workflow no longer starts a run (asking in your own words still works). acceptEdits mode now prompts before writing shell startup files (.zshenv, .bash_login) and build-tool configs that can execute code (.npmrc, .yarnrc, bunfig.toml, .bazelrc, .pre-commit-config.yaml, .devcontainer/). CLAUDE_CODE_OPUS_4_6_FAST_MODE_OVERRIDE is now a no-op.
entries.whyItMatters: If any script, alias, or onboarding doc tells people to type "workflow" to fan out agents, it silently stops triggering — rename to ultracode. The new acceptEdits prompts mean previously-unattended runs may now pause on config writes.

entries.title: WebFetch rules now override preapproved domains · sub-1s MCP timeouts no longer abort every call
entries.paragraph: Explicit WebFetch(domain:...) deny/ask/allow rules now take precedence over the built-in preapproved-host auto-allow. MCP per-server timeout values below 1000 ms were being floored to a 1-second watchdog that aborted every tool call; sub-1000 ms values are now ignored (falling back to MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT or the default). claude agents --json also gains a waitingFor field showing what a blocked session is waiting on.
entries.whyItMatters: If you leaned on the preapproved-domain auto-allow while also carrying an explicit WebFetch rule, the explicit rule now wins — re-check your allowlist. Any MCP server pinned to a sub-second timeout was failing every call and now works.

entries.title: Pin allowed versions with requiredMinimumVersion / requiredMaximumVersion · /plugin list
entries.paragraph: New managed settings requiredMinimumVersion and requiredMaximumVersion make Claude Code refuse to start outside the allowed range and point users to an approved version. Adds /plugin list with --enabled/--disabled filters. Stop and SubagentStop hooks can now return hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext to feed Claude context and keep the turn going without being flagged as a hook error. stdio MCP servers get the same CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID as hooks on --resume.
entries.whyItMatters: Version pinning gives admins a reproducible CLI baseline across a team. The Stop-hook additionalContext path lets you nudge the model after a turn without faking an error.

entries.title: fallbackModel setting · glob deny rules · relayed-message auth hardening
entries.paragraph: New fallbackModel setting configures up to three fallback models tried in order when the primary is overloaded or unavailable; --fallback-model now also applies to interactive sessions, and Claude Code retries a turn once on the fallback after an unexpected non-retryable API error. Deny rules accept glob patterns in the tool-name position ("*" denies all tools). Messages relayed via SendMessage from other sessions no longer carry user authority — receivers refuse relayed permission requests.
entries.whyItMatters: The fallback chain is a real resilience win for long unattended runs that previously died on a single overloaded-model error. The relayed-message change closes a cross-session privilege path worth knowing if you orchestrate multiple sessions.

entries.title: Fix: aborting during a PostToolUse hook no longer hangs the process
entries.paragraph: Hook callbacks were swallowing abort signals — aborting during a PostToolUse hook left the calling process hanging. It now ends the turn with a final result message.
entries.whyItMatters: If you wrap the SDK and cancel turns from hooks, you were at risk of a wedged process. One bump removes it.

entries.title: Native builds default to embedded find/grep · refusals carry stop_reason: "refusal"
entries.paragraph: On native builds, Agent SDK sessions now default to fast embedded find/grep in Bash (matching the interactive CLI) instead of always registering the dedicated Grep/Glob tools. To keep the dedicated tools — e.g. to intercept searches via canUseTool or hooks — name them in the tools option or allowedTools. Separately, refusal errors now carry stop_reason: "refusal" and stop_details on the assistant message and in transcripts.
entries.whyItMatters: If your host inspects or gates Grep/Glob calls, they may simply stop firing until you opt the tools back in. The refusal metadata lets you detect refusals without brittle text-matching.

example.code:
// keep dedicated search tools on native builds
query({ prompt, options: { allowedTools: ['Grep', 'Glob', /* ... */] } });

entries.title: stop_task idempotent for gone tasks · add builtin MCP servers via setMcpServers · hook additionalContext
entries.paragraph: stop_task control requests now return success when the target task is already not_found/not_running, so clients can prune stale task chips reliably. SDK hosts can add builtin MCP servers (e.g. claude-in-chrome) via setMcpServers even when the CLI launched without them. Stop and SubagentStop hooks support additionalContext in hookSpecificOutput.
entries.whyItMatters: The stop_task fix removes a race when tearing down fanned-out work; the setMcpServers fix lets you wire in builtin servers at runtime instead of only at launch.

entries.title: Fix: MCP resource tools now inject for servers added at runtime
entries.paragraph: Fixed MCP resource tools not being injected for servers added at runtime via the mcp_set_servers control request.
entries.whyItMatters: If you add MCP servers after session start and rely on their resource tools, they were silently missing until this release.

entries.title: Session archiving (/archive, codex archive) · clickable TUI markdown links · ChatGPT auth refresh hardening
entries.paragraph: Sessions can be archived from the TUI with /archive or the CLI with codex archive / codex unarchive; archived sessions are protected from resume/fork until restored. TUI markdown keeps web links clickable via OSC 8, and cramped tables fall back to readable key/value records. ChatGPT auth now refreshes tokens before the five-minute expiry window and shows a relogin path for reused refresh tokens instead of a generic cloud error. App-server integrations can resume a thread with its initial turns page and launch stdio mode with codex app-server --stdio.
entries.whyItMatters: Archiving lets you retire noisy sessions without deleting them. The auth-refresh change cuts spurious "cloud error" failures from expired ChatGPT tokens.

example.code:
codex archive    # retire a session (protected from resume/fork)
codex unarchive  # bring it back

entries.title: codex plugin list --json · parallel hosted web searches · enterprise credit limits & cloud-managed config
entries.paragraph: codex plugin list --json emits a machine-readable plugin inventory, and remote catalog suggestions are now cached. Standalone hosted web searches can run in parallel, and hosted web/image tools are available in more code-mode flows. Enterprise/admin flows show monthly credit limits and can apply cloud-managed config bundles (including EDU workspaces). Remote-control clients can start pairing and list or revoke controller grants via app-server v2 RPCs. TUI adds F13–F24 keybindings and paste in searchable menus.
entries.whyItMatters: plugin list --json is the hook for scripting plugin audits in CI. Cloud-managed config bundles let admins push a baseline config to a fleet instead of templating it by hand.

example.code: codex plugin list --json | jq '.[].name'   # script a plugin inventory

entries.title: Workload identity in audit logs · additional_tools in responses · migrate CLI removed
entries.paragraph: Adds workload identity to audit logs and an additional_tools item in responses, and makes ActionSearch.query optional. The bundled migrate CLI was removed.
entries.whyItMatters: If any tooling still shells out to the SDK's migrate CLI, it is gone in 6.40.0 — drop the call before you bump.

entries.title: Amazon Bedrock Responses support
entries.paragraph: Adds Amazon Bedrock support for the Responses API.
entries.whyItMatters: If you run the OpenAI Node SDK against Bedrock, the Responses API is now available there.

entries.title: Moderation on responses and chat.completions
entries.paragraph: Adds responses.moderation and chat_completions.moderation to the API surface.
entries.whyItMatters: You can run moderation inline against the Responses and Chat Completions flows without a separate client path.

suggestions.title: Re-check WebFetch permission rules after the 2.1.162 precedence change
suggestions.paragraph: As of Claude Code 2.1.162, explicit WebFetch(domain:...) deny/ask/allow rules take precedence over the built-in preapproved-host auto-allow. If your config mixes an explicit WebFetch rule with reliance on the preapproved-domain allowlist, the explicit rule now wins and may block or prompt for hosts that previously sailed through.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Permission changes are silent until a fetch you expected to work starts asking — or one you meant to block stops being blocked. Audit before it surprises a run.

example.code:
rg -F 'WebFetch(' .claude/settings.json .claude/settings.local.json
# reconcile explicit rules with the hosts you relied on auto-allowing

suggestions.tiesTo: claude-code · v2.1.162 — WebFetch rules override preapproved domains

suggestions.title: Opt Grep/Glob back in if your Agent SDK host intercepts searches
suggestions.paragraph: Agent SDK v0.3.162 makes native builds default to embedded find/grep in Bash instead of registering the dedicated Grep/Glob tools. If you gate or observe searches via canUseTool or hooks, those interceptors stop firing until you name the tools explicitly.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Your search guardrails can go dark with no error — the searches just route through Bash instead. Naming the tools restores the hook surface.
suggestions.tiesTo: Claude Agent SDK · v0.3.162 — native builds default to embedded find/grep

suggestions.title: Configure a fallbackModel chain for unattended runs
suggestions.paragraph: Claude Code 2.1.166 adds a fallbackModel setting that tries up to three models in order when the primary is overloaded or unavailable, and retries a turn once on the fallback after an unexpected non-retryable API error. Set it anywhere you run long or unattended sessions.
suggestions.whyItMatters: A single overloaded-model error used to kill an overnight or CI run; a fallback chain turns that into a transparent retry.

suggestions.title: Pin an approved Claude Code version range in managed settings
suggestions.paragraph: Claude Code 2.1.163 adds requiredMinimumVersion and requiredMaximumVersion managed settings — the CLI refuses to start outside the range and points users to an approved version. Use it to keep a team or CI fleet on a reproducible baseline.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Version drift across a team is a quiet source of flaky behavior; a pinned range removes it without policing installs by hand.

suggestions.title: Detect model refusals via stop_reason instead of matching text
suggestions.paragraph: Agent SDK v0.3.162 surfaces refusals with stop_reason: "refusal" and stop_details on the assistant message and in transcripts. If you currently sniff refusals by string-matching the error content, switch to the structured field.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Text-matching refusal copy breaks every time the wording changes; a stable stop_reason check does not.
suggestions.tiesTo: Claude Agent SDK · v0.3.162 — refusals carry stop_reason
